title: Reduce the effective interval onset to 2^751000000 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped analytic proof produced by Nick Petalas. Assuming alephnan's PR #6713 interval inequalities at `cd666f05c4e9006025b634687cc493911c8371c8`, retain the same uniform `10^-8` local-limit guarantee for every interval of length at most 5000, every real location and every endpoint convention:

```diff
- sufficient depth: n >= 2^(10^12)
+ sufficient depth: n >= 2^751000000
```

The new step proves `E(n,b) < 1025/(1024 log n)` for `log n >= 60` and `0 <= b <= 5000`. Multiplication by the inherited `c_sigma < 5` gives the exact upper bound `123/12304384000 < 1/100000000` at the new onset. Both the exact Gaussian-integral comparison and the left-endpoint Gaussian approximation are covered. The onset exponent decreases by a factor greater than 1331. Neither enormous integer is materialized.

This answers a small part of PR #6713's first open question. Its interval inequalities, six H hypotheses and classical analytic dependencies are cited mathematical premises. No predecessor program, certificate, convolution or numerical result is replayed or audited. Credit alephnan for those bounds, CubeJerry for PR #6329's fixed-height exponent, and the law/flow/analytic lineage named in PROOF.md.

## Evidence

Before: PR #6713 uses `2^(10^12)` for this local guarantee. After: PROOF.md bounds both decaying remainders by `1/(2048 log n)` apiece and proves the smaller sufficient onset by strict rational inequalities.

On CPython 3.12.15, normal and optimized checks both print `PASS_SMALLER_INTERVAL_ONSET`: 13 exact remainder gates, a positive onset cross-product slack of `548000000`, and two rejecting sufficient-certificate controls. The registered commands took 0.022 seconds each, rounded upward. The rejected smaller certificates are failures of this coarse sufficient estimate, not counterexamples to the underlying theorem.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/smaller-interval-onset/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/smaller-interval-onset/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/smaller-interval-onset
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/smaller-interval-onset --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Other hosts may substitute their CPython 3.12 executable. Both registered commands, development mode with warnings as errors, invalid-argument rejection, committed bytes/source ancestry/modes, and both read-only Git-free empty-PATH export replays passed. The generated receipt hashes all seven package files. Only this package is changed; the selected record and frozen sources retain their bytes.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The onset remains impractical. This is a scoped written analytic implication, not a new kappa, complete flow majorant, physical supplier or complete multiplication theorem. No predecessor replay, selected cold replay, physical compiler, native/ownership/precision/tape/recovery proof, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The five selected framework assumptions remain. The exact external source URL/hash identifies the cited mathematical premise; it is not represented as locally retained Git-history evidence.

## Open next questions

- Propagate the smaller local cutoff through the complete fixed-height flow proof, retaining all mixed layers, boundary exits and terminal leaves.
- Improve the error rate or constants with a sharper estimate of the actual characteristic function.

## Related open work

- #6713 supplies the effective interval inequalities and original local onset. This contribution derives a smaller sufficient onset from them.
- #6723 reviews the source interval inequalities and finite H premises. This contribution assumes those inequalities and adds a new quantitative consequence.
- #6728 reviews the literal paid-law tilt. This contribution does not recompute or change that tilt.
- #6729 reviews full mixed-layer propagation with the original cutoff. This contribution stops at the local bound and does not claim a new global majorant.
- #6741 reviews the finite capped-flow source law. This contribution uses no flow program or source histogram.
- #6742 checks complete capped-flow histograms. Those finite computations are separate from this analytic onset implication.
- #6743 bounds the nested compiler width policy for the same historical law. This contribution addresses local probability error, without changing that policy.
- #4547 repairs replay metadata for historical predecessors. This isolated package adopts no pending metadata repair.

Completion refresh examined the nine other open PRs from this account created since the CLAIM: #6785, #6786, #6788, #6789, #6790, #6791, #6792, #6793 and #6794. None studies this local-limit onset or the fixed raw-p7 law, so no additional related-work entry or numerical comparison was needed.
